title: Suite for Piano
program_note:
This collection of pieces for solo piano was begun in Philadelphia in the Spring, 1991, the bulk was written in Rochester in 1993-1994, and was finished in Los Angeles in December, 1994.  It is approximately 19’00” minutes long, with the individual movements 3’15”, 2’10”, 2’15”, 3’30”, 3’20”, and 4’15”.

The collection as a whole is in the form of an arch:  the first and last movements are paired, as are the second and fifth, and the third and fourth movements.  The outer movements are meant to rapid and somewhat flashy, and are built around shifting mirror inversions.  The second and fifth movements are influenced by jazz; the second by a twelve-bar blues (but with a metrical twist), and the fifth by the performance by Thelonius Monk of the song I Should Care.  The middle movements are essentially about different types of sonorities achievable on the piano; the third movement is all about opposing types of sonorities (short/long, loud/soft, high/low, etc.), while the fourth movement explores the possibilities of using a limited number of harmonies realized in a variety of ways on the piano.

Each movement may be performed individually, but the works make most sense as a set.  The outer movements clearly function as “opener” and “closer,” the middle two movements are somewhat more weighty, and the second and fifth movements can be thought of as serving the function of interludes between the weighty middle and the flashy outer movements.

David S. Lefkowitz

West Hollywood, CA

November 19, 1994
